capture_method: Native complete R4 model; exact AnimationPlayer seek; two complete renders to settle GPU skin upload; four shared-world camera views. Every clip start/end also compares a third draw pixel-for-pixel.
scope: Actual visual examination of each image row and all four views; quantitative mesh/collision distances are validated in separate native and Blender reports.
caveats: These close-up atlases have 384 by 448 pixels per direction. Submillimeter separations and intersections are assessed in the separate exact mesh and contact reports.
The isolated facial captures omit the target. Actual mouth-only contact timing, distance, and target surface alignment are checked separately in the native runtime and visible-demo fixture reports.
The rear direction reveals head, neck, and upper-back continuity; the facial surface is naturally occluded from that direction, and the prone upper back also occludes part of the lower rear neck.

atlases.observation: The standing bite opens in a closed-jaw snarl with teeth visible. The face, lips and jawline remain coherent as the head starts its anticipation; both side profiles preserve chin and cheek shape, and the rear neck/collar junction is stable.

The head rises slightly through anticipation and the lips begin changing toward the bite preparation. Teeth stay attached to the mouth, the cheek and chin silhouettes remain continuous, and no head/neck or collar pop appears.

The jaw starts opening progressively during anticipation. The upper lip and nose relationship stays stable while the lower teeth and chin move with the jaw; side profiles retain coherent cheek and jaw volume.

The mouth opens clearly as the head tilts into the bite windup. Upper and lower dental rows separate around a dark oral interior, with no floating teeth or obvious see-through cheek gap. The neck and shirt collar remain continuous.

The mouth reaches a broad open bite preparation: upper teeth remain anchored above the dark cavity and the lower teeth follow the lowered jaw. Both side profiles show a continuous chin/cheek outline rather than a detached lower face; the upper lip stays stable relative to the nose.

The head drives forward and downward into the bite while the jaw rapidly closes from its widest opening. Dental rows remain aligned with their lips, and the mouth corners, neck and collar remain coherent through the fast pre-contact change.

At the contact phase the jaw has closed into the snarl while the head remains thrust forward. Teeth and lips stay attached and aligned, the neck does not fold through the chin, and both side profiles preserve a solid jawline.

The closed-jaw follow-through holds before recovery. The face and lower jaw keep their shape without a morph pop; rear neck, collar and shoulder cloth remain continuous under the forward head posture.

The head begins easing out of its forward follow-through with the jaw closed. Lips and teeth remain registered to the face, and the chin-to-neck and collar silhouettes stay continuous across the recovery frames.
Recovery gradually reduces the head lean. The closed jaw retains its shape and teeth do not drift; both side profiles and the rear neck/upper-shirt surface show no sudden deformation change.
The head continues returning toward its guarded orientation. The closed snarl, cheek contour and jaw-to-neck transition remain stable; there is no late facial-shape rebound or collar discontinuity.

Late recovery holds the face in a coherent closed-mouth pose. Teeth, lips, chin and ears preserve their relative positions in the frontal and side views, while the rear neck and shirt junction remain stable.
The late standing recovery settles toward the opening snarl. Face and jaw proportions remain stable, with continuous lip, cheek and neck outlines and no final corrective-shape flicker.

The standing bite completes in its neutral closed-jaw expression. The endpoint matches the opening face and neck shape without a visible snap; teeth, lips and collar remain coherent through all four final frames.

The crawl bite begins in the correct low prone head posture from frame zero. The closed snarl and jawline are coherent in front and both side views; the extended neck remains connected to the collar without a standing-pose flash.

The low head prepares for the bite and the mouth begins to open near the end of this group. Cheek, chin and lip silhouettes remain stable despite the horizontal torso; the upper back naturally occludes the rear view of the lower neck.

The prone jaw opens progressively while the head stays low. The upper dental row remains anchored, the lower lip and teeth descend together, and the chin and cheek outline stays coherent in both side profiles.

The mouth holds its broad opening before the low bite lunge, then the head begins advancing. The dark oral cavity remains bounded by the lip and dental surfaces; no floating teeth, split cheek or obvious neck/collar intersection is visible.

The low head thrust finishes as the jaw closes quickly toward contact. Lower teeth and chin follow the closing motion together; the upper lip remains registered to the face, with no visible lip tearing or detached jaw edge.

At the prone contact phase the jaw is closed into its snarl while the head stays extended forward. The face and neck preserve solid side silhouettes, dental rows remain aligned, and the collar stays coherent beneath the low posture.

Closed-jaw follow-through remains low and forward. Teeth, lips, and jaw/chin side profiles stay coherent while the head holds briefly and body recovery starts. No mouth shape pop, cheek tear, or collar collision is visible. The prone upper back naturally occludes part of the rear neck.

The head gradually retracts from the prone bite follow-through toward its low resting guard. Closed mouth and snarl maintain registration; cheek/chin volume and neck/collar silhouettes remain continuous. No abrupt morph rebound or posture flash is visible.

Closed-jaw recovery continues in the low prone posture. The side profiles retain a solid chin and cheek silhouette; visible teeth stay registered in the narrow snarl. Small head and shoulder settling changes remain continuous, with no collar or neck flash in the four views.

Late prone recovery settles toward its resting head position. Lips, teeth, nose, and chin retain their alignment across the small nod and retraction. Shoulder cloth and the exposed neck line remain continuous; the rear view naturally shows the upper back instead of the mouth.

The mouth remains in its closed resting snarl through the final small settling motion. Side views keep stable jaw thickness, cheek contour, and neck attachment. Front tooth registration and both collar edges stay continuous across all six frames.

Final recovery approaches the initial prone guard without a visible facial or neck pop. The closed dental row, lips, chin, and brow remain coherent. No new cloth break, jaw rebound, or standing-pose flash appears in any direction.

The endpoint holds the closed, forward-facing prone snarl. Its head, jaw, and neck posture visually match the opening prone guard; the mouth stays registered and side profiles preserve volume. Four settled views show no endpoint discontinuity.

summary: All 82 standing bite poses and 73 prone bite poses were actually inspected in four directions, including every 60 Hz frame and both endpoints.

Each bite has a readable opening, forward lunge, mouth closure at contact, and closed-jaw recovery. Upper dental rows remain attached to the upper face, while the lower teeth, lip, and chin move together with the opening jaw.

The mouth interior remains bounded and dark during the open phases. No floating teeth, visible cheek tear, jaw collapse, collar collision, or prone-to-standing pose flash was observed at the reviewed pixel scale.
The closed recovery and endpoints preserve facial registration and continuous neck/collar silhouettes.
